### Declared by the engines themselves (69 modules state their limits)

* `cardmodel/anyps5/cards.py`: a debt card keeps the bullet's whole text (``text``, quoted from AnyPS5's docs so the classification can be recomputed from the cards alone); ``uses`` is resolved by C++ name as scan.py describes (an export's PS5 symbol is never matched, since AnyPS5's own code calls the host's function by that name), so it can include a same-named function from another file when no closer definition exists.
* `cardmodel/anyps5/classify.py`: a debt entry's cause comes from cue words in its text (the cards record which pattern matched), so a sentence that negates a cue ("measured, not inferred") can mislead it; the domain table is a judgement recorded in cards, not something read from AnyPS5.
* `cardmodel/anyps5/cover.py`: "complete" is relative to AnyPS5's own records, not to the console: a function nobody wrote a debt entry for can still differ from the PS5. The denominator is what AnyPS5 declares; 202 modules declare nothing, and the firmware's real export count is not read here (by policy).
* `cardmodel/anyps5/scan.py`: a lexical reading, not a compiler. Macros are not expanded, every #if branch is seen, member functions defined out of line are not indexed as helpers, call targets are resolved by name (same file, then same library, then a unique export anywhere), and a throw counts whether or not its condition can hold. The scan never runs AnyPS5 code and never writes into the checkout.
* `cardmodel/anyps5/witness.py`: the harness runs AnyPS5's code on this host's compiler and C++ library (the console runs its own build); unresolved symbols are left to dynamic lookup, so a check that reaches code outside the included sources fails loudly rather than silently; sampling is evidence on the inputs drawn, not a proof.
* `cardmodel/arcade/build.py`: one platform card so far (macOS); packages carry only the linker's ad-hoc signature; the store pictures are fixed moments of a scripted run, not chosen shots.
* `cardmodel/arcade/cli.py`: the launcher remembers a checkout's path (to start the service): after moving the repository, run `cardmodel arcade launcher --install` again. Installing from a linked git worktree points the launcher at the main checkout (a worktree is deleted with its session; `--home` names another checkout).
* `cardmodel/arcade/client.py`: this mirrors Launcher.swift (the native window and its page bridge are not driven; the launcher is checked by compiling it); a game counts as launched when its native executable runs the frames it was asked for, exits cleanly and draws a frame that is not one flat colour.
* `cardmodel/arcade/game.py`: the reference interpreter is far too slow for a software renderer's frames, so the engines compared on whole frames are the native and the Python emissions (short runs).
* `cardmodel/arcade/gen.py`: strings draw in the font card's upper-case ASCII (anything else is a blank); the equilibria are solved at neutral frame advantage for each fighter pair and distance, not for every state.
* `cardmodel/arcade/inventory.py`: counts are of cards, lines, functions and declarations, not of quality; a hand-written piece is named as such even where the model builds it, and nothing here measures how much fun the game is.
* `cardmodel/arcade/server.py`: localhost only and unauthenticated; one build at a time per game; card changes are seen through file times, code changes need a restart of the service.
* `cardmodel/cycle/evidence.py`: state is a cache (gitignored): a fresh checkout has none of these numbers until a cycle or a check has run there, and the goals that read them say "not run yet" until then.
* `cardmodel/cycle/hook.py`: "nothing changed" is a fingerprint of file sizes and times, so an edit that keeps both is seen only after max_interval_s; the background cycle runs at a lower priority but still uses CPU and memory while you work; the schedule installs for the current user only.
* `cardmodel/cycle/ledger.py`: the ledger sees names, statements and targets, not behaviour. A law whose witness test is gutted keeps its hash (the cycle's ``laws`` stage runs every witness for that); a command that still parses but no longer works is the tests' business.
* `cardmodel/cycle/report.py`: regressions compare with the previous run only (not a trend), and seeded witnesses differ between runs by design, so a moved count is a regression only where the metric is deterministic; the shortfall lists are read from the engines' docstrings and the ROADMAP, so they are as current as those texts.
* `cardmodel/cycle/run.py`: the deadline is a timer signal, so it interrupts Python code but not one long call inside C (a single huge integer operation finishes first); it needs the main thread (elsewhere stages run unbounded and the budget is checked between them); the lock is advisory (flock on the system's temporary folder), so it coordinates the processes of one machine only.
* `cardmodel/cycle/stages.py`: stages share this process except laws and tests (a child each); a stage the budget cannot fit is skipped and says so; the cycle never promotes the model's own internal calls into the model (names of its own helpers would only flatter its named fraction), and it keeps arena runs and measurements in its state instead of writing a card per run.
* `cardmodel/cycle/witness_runner.py`: a test that kills the interpreter (a segfault, os._exit) loses every outcome after it, and the caller sees those ids as not reported.
* `cardmodel/emit/lean.py`: without Mathlib, nonlinear facts beyond ``grind``'s ring normaliser stay unproved; a statement is emitted for every rule regardless.
* `cardmodel/emit/lean_chain.py`: integer equations over the operators the rule theorems cover (+ - * ^ // % and unary -); rules with side conditions are not used; the search is bounded (depth, nodes), so "no chain" is not a disproof.
* `cardmodel/emit/lean_import.py`: statements are reproduced, not proofs (a proof is checked by citing the original); ``∃``, structures, lists, sets, instances and higher-order statements are outside the fragment; the witness samples values.
* `cardmodel/emit/lean_logic.py`: aggregates, function calls, floats and negation of derived (IDB) predicates are not encoded (reported per fact as ``not_exportable`` with the reason); an argument position must hold either symbols or integers, not both; existential variables under negation must range over symbols.
* `cardmodel/engines/arena.py`: the arena knows the answer only for the kinds it planted; speedups are in-process CPython timings on this machine; a decoy can be *correctly* substituted by a different card (e.g. range(1, n) sums are triangular numbers) and that is not counted as an error.
* `cardmodel/engines/codefacts.py`: syntactic: calls through variables, decorators and dynamic dispatch are not resolved; effects are recognised by name (open/print/socket/requests/time/random/os/subprocess, global statements, attribute and subscript assignment); classes contribute their methods as ``Class.method``.
* `cardmodel/engines/codegen.py`: templates are only as right as the conformance matrix that checks them; identifiers are renamed only for the language card's ``reserved`` list; emitted code is plain (no formatting pass).
* `cardmodel/engines/conformance.py`: sampling, not proof; inputs stay inside each op's declared domain and, for fixed-width languages, inside the int width.
* `cardmodel/engines/exprs.py`: no complex numbers (``I``), no symbolic simplification; names outside the whitelist raise ``UnknownName`` (fail closed).
* `cardmodel/engines/frontend_python.py`: no strings, lists, dicts, classes, exceptions, globals, closures or side effects; ``int`` follows Python's unbounded semantics, so fixed-width targets agree only inside the declared input domain.
* `cardmodel/engines/funcalg.py`: functions of one integer variable; behaviours that are not linear recurrences of order <= MAX_ORDER on the sampled range (exponentials of n^2, primes, ...) have no canonical form here; "checked" is evidence on sampled terms, proof comes from the algebra of the fitted form (exact rational arithmetic) only for the fitted range.
* `cardmodel/engines/improve.py`: equivalence is sampled, not proven; behavioural matching only finds algorithms that have a card; timing is in-process Python on this machine; module-level code is never executed (only function definitions are, to test them).
* `cardmodel/engines/laws.py`: only these templates; witnesses sample the integers (edges included); bit operators have no Lean form in core, so those laws stay ``witnessed``.
* `cardmodel/engines/learn.py`: call cards learned this way are names with evidence of use, not semantics; function domains are inferred heuristically; a rejected proposal is kept, not deleted, so it can be revisited.
* `cardmodel/engines/logic.py`: terms are constants (symbols, integers, floats): no function symbols, so no lists or trees as values. Bindings can create new values, so evaluation has a fact budget (L20) and raises LogicLimit instead of running forever. Negation and aggregation use the closed world of the strata below them. Booleans are stored as the symbols true/false (Python would conflate True with 1).
* `cardmodel/engines/mine.py`: only these templates (rules of length <= 2 over unary and binary relations); a law of the data is evidence about this data, not a proof about the world; quadratic in the number of relations for compose.
* `cardmodel/engines/observe.py`: static only (no runtime types); non-Python languages are token-level estimates, not parses; aliases (``from m import f as g``) are not resolved.
* `cardmodel/engines/optimize.py`: timings depend on this machine and its load; Python in-process timings include call overhead; compiled per-call costs are a slope over two runs, not a cycle count.
* `cardmodel/engines/probes.py`: a passing probe says the tool starts and reports a version; it does not prove every feature works. That is what witnesses are for.
* `cardmodel/engines/redefs.py`: numeric agreement on sampled points is evidence, not proof. For non-rational forms the float screen can still hide a difference below its tolerance, and the high-precision decision is a convergence test, not interval arithmetic: a discontinuous step (floor, a comparison) taken on a transcendental value that sits exactly on the jump can be misjudged at every precision.
* `cardmodel/engines/rewrite.py`: anchors are heuristic until ``cardmodel optimize`` measures them; domain matching is by name and declared parents only.
* `cardmodel/engines/runners.py`: forms run with the user's privileges (no sandbox): only run card code you trust; the build cache is keyed by source text, so a new seed (new baked inputs) means a new compile.
* `cardmodel/engines/search.py`: bounded breadth-first search, so a proof that needs more steps than ``max_depth`` (or more nodes than ``max_nodes``) is reported as not found -- that is not a disproof. Side conditions on rules (e.g. ``k >= 0``) are checked by the numeric witness, not during search.
* `cardmodel/engines/selfcheck.py`: the sandbox check needs macOS ``sandbox-exec``; elsewhere only the static check runs and the result says so.
* `cardmodel/engines/selflogic.py`: these facts cover the fields above, not every field of every card; the theory checks what its rules say and nothing else (the kernel's schema validation is still the authority on shapes).
* `cardmodel/engines/theorems.py`: witnesses sample; they do not prove. Lean proofs use core tactics only (decide, omega, grind, simp; no Mathlib), so nonlinear or inductive facts may stay ``witnessed``. Statements calling card-language functions are witnessed but not sent to Lean (codegen emits ``partial def``, which proofs cannot unfold).
* `cardmodel/engines/translate.py`: equivalence is sampled (seed printed); domains are heuristic until a person or a learned card narrows them; only the frontend's subset lifts (see frontend_python).
* `cardmodel/engines/witness.py`: sampling, not proof; documentation-only forms are reported as such and never counted as verified.
* `cardmodel/game/ai.py`: one-exchange lookahead (no search over the duel tree); seeded, so a run is reproducible.
* `cardmodel/game/analysis.py`: one exchange at a time (the matrix game of a state, not the whole duel tree); the equilibrium is one of possibly many (sensitivity therefore measures exploitability, which does not depend on which equilibrium the solver returns).
* `cardmodel/game/combat.py`: distance is three bands; movement inside an exchange is one band per step; there are no multi-hit strings or projectiles yet; values are integers (deterministic, replayable).
* `cardmodel/game/world.py`: discrete ticks; a fact's first derivation per tick is its recorded cause (other causes may also exist); impact counts differing facts, it does not weigh them.
* `cardmodel/kernel/resources.py`: the watchdog samples every POLL_S seconds, so a child can briefly exceed its cap between samples; peak memory (ru_maxrss) never goes down, so once the self cap trips this process stays tripped.
* `cardmodel/kernel/schema.py`: no remote $ref, no $dynamicRef, no if/then/else, no dependentSchemas, no unevaluatedProperties. ``format`` checks only the three formats listed. Errors are reported as "path: message" strings.
* `cardmodel/lang/compile.py`: no strings, lists or user types inside functions; the ``Nat`` type is a domain annotation (an int >= 0), not truncating arithmetic; a ``match`` substitutes the scrutinee into each arm (it is re-evaluated, which is fine for pure expressions); an effectful call may not sit in the lazy operand of ``and``/``or``/``if-then-else`` (write an ``if`` statement).
* `cardmodel/lang/run.py`: function verification inputs come from the ``requires`` contract (bounds on parameters) or a small default range; tests and queries see the closed world of the module (and the modules it ``use``s).
* `cardmodel/lang/syntax.py`: no user-defined types, strings, lists or closures in functions (the IR's int/float/bool subset; see ROADMAP); no operator overloading; errors stop at the first syntax error in a declaration.
* `cardmodel/machine/asm.py`: no expressions, macros or sections; a label used before its definition must be in the same assembly; ``e`` targets must be within -128..127 of the next instruction.
* `cardmodel/machine/bench.py`: this checks the cards against their own data and against each other's engines, plus the hand-derived vectors; it is not an independent oracle of the real CPU. Test ROMs (cpu_instrs, mooneye) are.
* `cardmodel/machine/build.py`: one ISA per machine (a two-CPU machine such as the DS composes two modules); components are concatenated in card order and share one namespace, so two components may not define the same name (the compiler reports it).
* `cardmodel/machine/diff.py`: equal hashes on these frames are evidence for this input, not a proof for every input; the script presses START and A periodically (survey.script).
* `cardmodel/machine/gb.py`: MMM01, MBC6, MBC7, HuC1/HuC3, TAMA5 and the camera are reported as unsupported (the game runs as ROM-only and will likely misbehave); no boot ROM (the documented post-boot state is used, so DMG games on a CGB get no colourisation palette: they run in DMG mode).
* `cardmodel/machine/isa.py`: decode by opcode byte (+ prefix byte) only; ISAs decoded by bit masks (ARM) use ``mask_dispatch_source``. The stored IR is what every engine runs; the semantics text is its source.
* `cardmodel/machine/lift.py`: code in RAM, code after EI and the HALT/STOP/illegal opcodes always run in the interpreter; a key is (ROM offset, which half of the address space), so a bank mapped at an unusual place gets its own blocks; MBC1 multicart remapping is treated like any bank.
* `cardmodel/machine/lift_arm.py`: ARM state on the ARM9 only (Thumb and the ARM7 stay interpreted); a block ends at every instruction that may write R15; the guards read every word through the bus, so for RAM-resident code a block costs about what the interpreter's fetches cost (the decode is what it saves).
* `cardmodel/machine/native.py`: a ``cabi`` machine runs with the user's privileges like any compiled code, and an index out of range is undefined behaviour there (machine code masks every index; the reference interpreter checks).
* `cardmodel/machine/nds.py`: no 2D/3D graphics, sound, touch, firmware/SPI, RTC or Wi-Fi; no wait states (a nominal instructions-per-line budget); WRAM and VRAM banking are flat; nothing here decrypts anything: an image whose secure area is encrypted is refused.
* `cardmodel/machine/shell.py`: audio is streamed in frame-sized chunks with a small jitter buffer (a late chunk is dropped, not stretched); one machine per server; the page binds 127.0.0.1 only.
* `cardmodel/machine/survey.py`: a scripted input cannot play a game, so "runs" means it boots and animates; games that wait for a specific button sequence show up as ``static``.
* `cardmodel/machine/testroms.py`: a timeout is a failure to report, not a pass; a DMG test meant for a CGB in its DMG-compatibility mode is skipped (that mode is not modelled).
